question: Will any state actor use chemical weapons in Ukraine before May 1, 2026?
summary: Ensemble aggregate: 65% probability of state-actor chemical weapons use in Ukraine before May 1, 2026.
Objections highlight attribution uncertainty, deterrence effects, and practical escalation barriers as downward pressures on near-term risk.
Threshold-breach argument in the adversarial analysis is not uniformly credible; it is not relied upon to justify a higher probability.

justification.critique_assessment: Yes, objections are valid in identifying attribution uncertainty and deterrence as downward pressures, while acknowledging non-zero risk remains.
justification.adjustment: Adjusted downward from 0.65 to 0.58 to reflect deterrence, attribution uncertainty, and escalation barriers; did not rely on the threshold-breach claim, which was deemed implausible as a sole basis for increasing probability.

forecasts.reference-class: Baseline probability of state-actor use of chemical weapons in modern interstate/conflict contexts (historically rare but not unheard of; current Ukraine-specific risk is elevated by repeated incidents and intel assessments).

sources.claim: OPCW confirms presence of the riot control agent CS in three incidents along Ukrainian frontlines (Dnipropetrovsk region) from October 2024.
OPCW reports further evidence of chemical weapons use in Ukraine (CS) in a February 14, 2025 report; Grenades and related materials analyzed with CS-related findings.
Dutch and German intelligence say Russia has stepped up use of banned chemical weapons in Ukraine, including chloropicrin and CS; described as standardized.
CBS/AP reporting that Dutch and German intelligence say Russia is increasing use of banned chemical weapons (chloropicrin and CS) in Ukraine.
UK sanctions Russian troops for deploying chemical weapons on the battlefield in Ukraine, including chloropicrin; cites violation of the Chemical Weapons Convention.
Guardian reporting on ongoing accusations of chemical gas attacks in Ukraine; context includes US/UK statements and OPCW involvement.
OPCW and UK collaboration to support Ukraine's chemical weapons threat monitoring; demonstrates continued oversight in Ukraine.
DW reports that both Russia and Ukraine are accused of using outlawed weapons; U.S. has accused Russia of chemical weapon use in Ukraine.
OPCW confirms CS riot-control agent presence from a 2024 incident along frontlines in Ukraine after a Technical Assistance Visit; analyzes samples and emphasizes prohibition of chemical weapons use.
OPCW reports additional chemical weapons use in Ukraine (CS) in 2025; attribution to a specific actor not identified in the report.
OPCW visited Ukraine over chemical weapons allegations; Ukraine alleged Russia used riot-control agents; no formal attribution provided in the public account.
Dutch and German intelligence report increased use of banned chemical weapons by Russia in Ukraine (chloropicrin and CS); claims normalization of such use; OPCW hasn't published a full attribution.

OPCW transmitted a report confirming the presence of the riot-control agent CS in three October 2024 incidents along Ukraine's front lines; independent laboratories corroborated CS and related compounds in grenades and environmental samples.
OPCW found more evidence of chemical weapons use in Ukraine (CS in all three October 2024 incidents); the report did not identify the responsible party.
Ukraine's Foreign Ministry says 6,129 cases of munitions containing hazardous chemicals were recorded since February 2023, with CS and CN detected, citing OPCW findings and Ukrainian samples.

Dutch intelligence agencies say Russia has stepped up use of prohibited chemical weapons in Ukraine, including chloropicrin and riot-control agent CS; OPCW has identified CS incidents but has not conducted a full investigation.
